title: The Room Between Us
summary: Why the closest relationships need a little space: two people who share every edge blur into one, and the gap between them is what keeps both whole.
cast: two facing profiles ('faces'), a single profile, and two walkers (one-line figures, no features inside the face)

pages.section: Hook: how close is too close?
pages.say: Two people who love each other lean in, closer and closer. It feels like the goal is to close the gap completely. So why do the closest people still need room?

beats.action: the pen draws one brow, nose and chin, then loops over to draw the second facing it
the two profiles lean in until the gap between them is a narrow sliver
swells in behind the two faces

beats.object: the narrow gap between the noses
beats.action: the pen rests at the gap as the question lands beside it

pages.section: Intuition: share every edge and the lines run together
pages.say: When two people share every edge, every plan, friend and evening, their outlines start to touch. Then they overlap. Soon you can't tell which line belongs to whom.

beats.action: held from the last page, they press forward until nose meets nose
melt into each other and curl into a tangle of one line
the pen circles the tangle once more, tightening it

pages.section: Mechanism: one line slowly serves two
pages.say: It happens quietly. One person drops a hobby, then a friend, then an opinion, to keep the peace. Untangle it, and only one face is left.

beats.action: held from the last page, it loosens at one end
one loop winds back into the pen and is gone
the tangle straightens into one profile so large its chin runs off the bottom of the frame
the profile faces nothing as the caption settles on the bare side

pages.section: Turn: the gap itself is a shape
pages.say: In 1915 the psychologist Edgar Rubin drew two faces with a gap between them. Look again, and the gap is a vase. The space between two people is something too: it holds things.

beats.action: held from the last page, it unwinds and redraws as two facing profiles with a clear gap
the pen finishes the second chin, the gap now shaped like a vase
swells in inside the gap so the vase between the faces glows
the camera eases back to show both faces and the gap whole

pages.say: Room looks ordinary. A walk on your own, a friend who is only yours, an evening with a book. Each person walks their own road, and comes back with something new to tell.

beats.action: unwind into a long horizon line across the paper

beats.object: a small walker beside a big mountain
beats.action: the line climbs into a mountain and a small walker steps out at its foot
swells in behind the mountain peak like open sky
the horizon runs on and draws a second walker heading back toward the first

pages.section: Close: close enough to see, far enough to stay whole
pages.say: So keep the gap. Close enough to see each other clearly, far enough that both faces stay whole.

beats.action: the walkers rise and turn into the two facing profiles from the first page, with the vase-shaped gap between them
swells in behind both faces, warm again
the pen closes the last chin and lifts away, leaving both faces complete
